subject.title: Feature: Streaming TTS pipeline for voice calls (sentence-level LLM→TTS→audio)

question: Should classic Voice Call gain a provider-generic sentence-level streaming contract, and which speech-provider/carrier pair should be the first supported reference implementation?
rationale: The feature crosses plugin speech APIs, embedded-agent partial delivery, carrier playback, and irreversible partial-audio recovery; current main only supplies narrower latency fixes, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent contract or rollout scope.

options.title: Provider-generic contract first
options.body: Add an optional streaming speech capability and implement one reference provider/carrier pair with conformance, fallback, and live latency proof.

options.title: Twilio-specific implementation
options.body: Ship a Voice Call-local Twilio path sooner, accepting later API refactoring and uneven Telnyx or provider behavior.

options.title: Realtime-only strategy
options.body: Keep the classic path buffered and direct latency-sensitive deployments to full-duplex OpenAI or Gemini realtime voice.

recommendation.title: Provider-generic contract first
recommendation.body: Add an optional streaming speech capability and implement one reference provider/carrier pair with conformance, fallback, and live latency proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent feature history and merge activity place them closest to the classic response, carrier playback, and realtime-versus-classic product boundary.
